genZNote: Grows at fridge temperatures well enough that cold enrichment is an actual isolation technique built around it.

habitat.naturalHabitat: GI tract of many domestic and wild animals, especially pigs
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Psychrotrophic — able to grow at refrigeration temperatures, contaminated pork products a classic source

culture.growthCharacteristics: Grows at refrigeration temperature (cold enrichment technique aids isolation)
culture.colonyMorphology: "Bull's-eye" colonies (dark red center, translucent rim) on CIN agar

identificationClues: Grows at refrigeration temperatures — cold enrichment technique improves recovery from stool
Can mimic acute appendicitis ("pseudoappendicitis") due to mesenteric lymphadenitis

clinicalImportance.transmission: Foodborne — undercooked pork is a classic source; also unpasteurized milk and contaminated water
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: An important cause of foodborne enterocolitis, particularly associated with pork products; notable for its ability to grow at refrigerator temperatures on contaminated food
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Cold enrichment (holding stool specimen at 4°C before subculturing) increases yield since the organism outcompetes normal flora better at low temperature

examFacts.importantTest: Cold enrichment culture; CIN agar bull's-eye colonies
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Grows at refrigerator temperatures, enabling cold enrichment for isolation
